name: create_server_c
description: Creates a basic TCP echo server in C
prompts: Create a simple TCP echo server in C. Save it as server.c. It should listen on port 8080, accept one connection, echo back whatever the client sends, then exit.

test_setup_files.test_server.py:
import subprocess, socket, time
subprocess.run(['gcc', 'server.c', '-o', 'server_bin'], check=True)
srv = subprocess.Popen(['./server_bin'])
try:
    conn = None
    for _ in range(20):
        try:
            conn = socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 8080), timeout=1)
            break
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(0.5)
    assert conn is not None, 'could not connect to 127.0.0.1:8080 within 10s'
    msg = b'hello-optarena'
    conn.sendall(msg)
    conn.settimeout(5)
    data = conn.recv(1024)
    conn.close()
    assert data == msg, f'expected echo {msg!r}, got {data!r}'
finally:
    srv.terminate()
    try:
        srv.wait(timeout=5)
    except Exception:
        srv.kill()
print('PASS')
